meta.title: Context manager
meta.description: Session context management plugin: adds a Context manager entry (the list icon on the right of the session header) to the session header and manages the model context of a DSH session — delete messages one by one or whole turns, and restore them later. Two typical uses: roll back to the start of a turn and ask again (use /ctxmgr turns to read the turn numbers, then /ctxmgr deleteturn 5 to move that whole turn out of the context), and drop noise such as error logs, pasted code and trial-and-error instructions entry by entry (use /ctxmgr list to find the indexes, then /ctxmgr delete 12,13,14). The context_manager tool offers the same operations (actions list / list-turns / delete / delete-turns / restore). Deleting appends an empty developer message (a tombstone) that replaces the range on the session surface, so the raw session log, the chat transcript and audit data stay intact and removed messages disappear only from later model requests. Turns are listed with numbers, previews and an in-progress marker. Operations that cannot append safely are written into the session log as plugin records and applied at the next request, so they survive restarts; restore puts user and context messages back at their original position and appends assistant content at the tail. Local only, nothing leaves the machine. Requires a running session; system prompts and messages that are still streaming cannot be deleted. Turning the plugin off removes the header entry, the command and the tool, while tombstones already written stay in the log. Message rows and the total occupation show heuristic token estimates (4 characters ≈ 1 token; Chinese text and JSON are markedly underestimated; the Host prefers node pricing from ctx.tokenMeter when available). A new /ctxmgr clean <target tokens> command and the context_manager action clean trim the largest tool and assistant messages down to a token budget: user and context messages are never eligible, the most recent 3 messages are protected by default, candidates below 100 tokens are skipped, and deletions still go through the restorable tombstone and queue pipeline. It also keeps a batch ledger: every delete, whole-turn delete, clean and undo mints a batch id and appends an append-only plugin:context-manager/batch record to the session log (viewable with /ctxmgr batches, still there after a restart, no external files), and /ctxmgr undo-batch undoes the latest operation or a specific batch by batch-id prefix through the existing restore path. Not the same plugin as the same-named @sulytwelve/dsh-context-manager: this one only does reversible, in-place trimming of the exact selection inside the current session — no cross-session memory, no global compression engine, no dashboard. Each tombstone source also carries a tiny recall pointer: at most 8 entries, previews truncated to 80 characters, storing only seq / role / a one-line preview and never the full message text. Deleting therefore unloads content from the main context into a searchable archive instead of erasing it: the read-only session_event_search tool of @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-session-query can find it by keyword, and session_event_read returns the complete original event for a seq (searches exclude the caller session and are authorized by the workspace cwd). A new /ctxmgr compact <start> <end> command and context_manager action compact (parameters start / end) hand only the user selection to the official ctx.compaction.compactRegion for one summary — start / end are surface position seqs whose edges must be tool-pair balanced, a loaded compaction backend such as dsh-compaction-basic is required, no global threshold compaction is performed, and both success and failure are recorded in the ledger. The dialog gains a filter dropdown (all / user / assistant / tool / context) that only affects display while selection and token totals stay unchanged, and user message rows carry a protected marker.
